section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses self-compassion as a within-persons protective factor in relation to body image and eating behaviors. It reviews two key daily diary studies: Study 1 (Breines et al. 2014) with college women over four days, and Study 2 (Kelly & Stephen 2016) with college women over seven days. Both studies found that when participants experienced higher-than-usual self-compassion, they reported better body image outcomes and more adaptive eating behaviors, suggesting that fluctuations in self-compassion within individuals are associated with variability in body image and eating experiences.
